facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: On the supplied filings, Magnite's financial base is strong and simple. Debt is a single secured term loan with principal of $357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, an undrawn $175.0 million revolver and cash of $392,862 thousand. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, gross leverage is 1.27x and net leverage is -0.13x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, down from 2.89x and 0.43x at FY2024, and cash-paid-interest cover is 10.98x. On a stricter base of income from operations plus depreciation and amortization (which carries stock compensation as an expense), gross leverage is 1.81x. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 is $551,127 thousand against $474,583 thousand, and CTV is the growth driver. The main qualifications are that cash is partly working-capital float (payables of $1,738,299 thousand against cash of $392,862 thousand) and swung from $553,362 thousand at FY2025 to $184,648 thousand at Q1 2026 before recovering, that FY2025 net income of $144,613 thousand includes a one-off income tax benefit of $73,986 thousand, and that covenant terms rest on the filings' description, not the credit agreement.

Only the term loan remains; the convertible notes were repaid in March 2026, cutting principal from $565,521 thousand to $359,546 thousand.
Adjusted EBITDA rose from $232,131 thousand in FY2025 to $280,586 thousand over the last twelve months, while income from operations plus depreciation gives a lower base.
Cash of $392,862 thousand sits beside payables of $1,738,299 thousand, and first-quarter operating cash flow was negative.
The October 2026 repricing lowers the term loan margin to 2.50% and is a subsequent event not in September balances.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Magnite is a public company with no financial sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources and a single operating segment. It sells technology that lets publishers, especially connected TV owners, monetize ad inventory to buyers and demand-side platforms, and earns a fee that is a percentage of the ad spend. The credit-relevant business facts are the dependence on a small number of large demand sources, the concentration of connected TV supply in a few large sellers, the lower fees on reserve auctions, seasonal fourth-quarter strength, and the effect of the Google antitrust ruling on open-web display competition. The credit-relevant history is the financing of the SpotX acquisition by a term loan and convertible notes, the 2024 refinancing and repricings, the repayment of the convertible notes in cash at maturity in March 2026, and the October 2026 repricing amendment. There is no pending acquisition, sponsor transaction or new debt issue in the supplied sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: deleveraging by repayment, share repurchases under a board plan and no dividends. The financial consequences are in the accepted financial base handoff; the main limits here are that ownership percentages, the proxy statement and the executed financing documents are not supplied, and that operating claims in the releases are management language.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue is a percentage of ad spend and the take rate "tends to be lower on CTV transactions" (10K p41); results are higher in the fourth quarter (10K p29). Mechanic: growth is volume driven and exposed to ad budgets and to fee compression as connected TV reserve auctions grow. Implication: cash flow is cyclical and seasonal; the financial base shows strong recent growth, but revenue visibility is not contractually evidenced (Insufficient Information on contract terms). The Google remedies are a possible counter-force but are unquantified and under appeal. 2. Concentration risk. Evidence: "two buyers accounted for 40% and 12%" of receivables (10K p137) and demand is "highly concentrated among relatively few DSPs" (10K p25). Mechanic: a payment delay or volume shift at one platform hits both collections and revenue, and Magnite pays sellers regardless. Implication: liquidity and the cash-float qualification matter more than the leverage ratio alone. 3. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor named; no dividends; notes repaid from cash. Mechanic: no sponsor extraction channel is evidenced. Implication: monitor share repurchases against the credit agreement restrictions, which are not supplied. 4. Key uncertainties: executed financing documents, proxy ownership, contract terms and the outcome and timing of the Google remedies and damages claim.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Magnite is a low-leverage, cash-rich credit with one secured term loan, and the supplied evidence supports a strong but cyclical view with Medium confidence. The strongest support is that gross debt of USD 357,730 thousand is 1.27x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, cash of USD 392,862 thousand exceeds it, the revolver is undrawn and no debt matures before February 2029 [CP-1]. The weakest point is that earnings follow advertising budgets, depend on a few demand platforms and sit beside large seller payables, so reported cash overstates free liquidity [CP-1, CP-1A]. The outcome turns on whether connected TV volume growth outruns fee compression and whether cash returns to shareholders stay modest, and the credit agreement terms that would limit them are not supplied [CP-0].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Magnite's capital structure is the simplest part of the credit. Since the convertible senior notes were repaid from cash at maturity on March 15, 2026, the only debt is the 2024 term loan, with principal of USD 357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, scheduled amortization of USD 3,632 thousand a year, and USD 342,294 thousand falling due after 2030, at the February 2031 maturity [CP-1]. The USD 175.0 million revolver matures in February 2029, was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end, and had USD 170.9 million available after USD 4.1 million of letters of credit. The October 7, 2026 repricing, a subsequent event, cut the term loan margin to Term SOFR plus 2.50%; at the September 30, 2026 principal that is roughly USD 1,789 thousand a year of lower interest before changes in Term SOFR [CP-1, calculation 11].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Cash is the item most open to misreading. The company collects from buyers and pays sellers, and the filing states that "in the event a buyer defaults on payment, we may still be required to pay sellers for the inventory purchased" [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Two buyers made up 40% and 12% of receivables at December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Cash fell from USD 553,362 thousand at FY2025 to USD 184,648 thousand at the end of the first quarter, helped by the USD 205,067 thousand note repayment and a negative first-quarter operating cash flow, before recovering to USD 392,862 thousand [CP-1]. Net debt of USD -35,132 thousand is therefore a point-in-time figure, not a permanent surplus.

facts.text: The leverage covenant is a springing test: First Lien Net Leverage Ratio below 3.25 to 1.00, tested at quarter end only if revolver utilization exceeds 35% of commitments [Q3 2026 10-Q]. As an indicator only, not the covenant calculation, first-lien debt at the term loan principal would reach 3.25x of LTM Adjusted EBITDA only if that EBITDA fell by about 61%, with cash netting and the covenant EBITDA definition both unknown [CP-0].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main strengths are balance-sheet capacity and growth momentum. Gross leverage of 1.27x on Adjusted EBITDA, net cash after the March 2026 repayment, an undrawn USD 175.0 million revolver, no maturity before 2029 and interest cover of 10.98x leave wide room against the one springing covenant [CP-1]. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 was USD 551,127 thousand against USD 474,583 thousand a year earlier, led by connected TV [CP-1]. The absence of a financial sponsor, dividends or debt-funded distributions in the sources read, and the repayment of the convertible notes without new borrowing, are supportive behaviours [CP-1A]. The Google ruling is a potential tailwind to open-web display share, though it is management's expectation, unquantified and under appeal.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main weaknesses are cyclicality, concentration and unverified terms. Revenue is a percentage of ad spend, with lower fees on connected TV reserve auctions, so growth in the fastest channel can dilute the fee rate [CP-1A]. Demand is concentrated in a few platforms and two buyers hold over half of receivables, so a payment delay or loss would hit revenue and cash together. Cash includes publisher and customer float, seasonality lifts the fourth quarter, and first-quarter cash flow can be negative [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock compensation of USD 76,648 thousand in FY2025. The credit agreement, covenant definitions, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so legal capacity to add debt or distribute cash cannot be tested [CP-0, CP-1A]. Business is one segment, so no other activity offsets a weak ad market.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Revolver utilization trigger: 35% x USD 175,000 thousand = USD 61,250 thousand (Q3Q p20 for the 35% and 175.0 million commitment). Q2 2026 draw: USD 60,000 thousand, equal to 34.3% of commitments (60,000 / 175,000). Whether letters of credit of USD 4,100 thousand add to utilization (which would give 36.6%) is not stated. 2. Indicator headroom, not the covenant: 357,730 / 3.25 = 110,071 of EBITDA at which gross term loan leverage equals 3.25x; 1 - 110,071 / 280,586 = 60.8% fall from LTM Adjusted EBITDA (280,586 from CP-1). The covenant ratio is net of cash and uses a defined EBITDA, both unknown. 3. Total liquidity components shown separately, not netted for float: cash 392,862 plus undrawn revolver 170,900 = 563,762. 4. Lease liabilities: 21,558 + 40,436 = 61,994 (Q3Q p2). 5. All other figures are from CP-1 (leverage 1.27x and 1.81x, net debt -35,132, cover 10.98x, LTM Adjusted EBITDA 280,586) and are not recomputed.

### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Magnite is lightly levered on issuer-defined Adjusted EBITDA: gross debt of $357,730 thousand is 1.27x last-twelve-months EBITDA, and cash exceeds debt. ### Financial base view

On the supplied filings, Magnite's financial base is strong and simple. Debt is a single secured term loan with principal of $357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, an undrawn $175.0 million revolver and cash of $392,862 thousand. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back stock-based compensation, gross leverage is 1.27x and net leverage is -0.13x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026, down from 2.89x and 0.43x at FY2024, and cash-paid-interest cover is 10.98x. On a stricter base of income from operations plus depreciation and amortization (which carries stock compensation as an expense), gross leverage is 1.81x. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 is $551,127 thousand against $474,583 thousand, and CTV is the growth driver. The main qualifications are that cash is partly working-capital float (payables of $1,738,299 thousand against cash of $392,862 thousand) and swung from $553,362 thousand at FY2025 to $184,648 thousand at Q1 2026 before recovering, that FY2025 net income of $144,613 thousand includes a one-off income tax benefit of $73,986 thousand, and that covenant terms rest on the filings' description, not the credit agreement.

#### Contribution ex-TAC by channel

CTV Contribution ex-TAC was "CTV $ 304,192 $ 260,159 $ 218,494" for FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 (10K p98) and "CTV $ 105,368 $ 75,847 39 % $ 284,770 $ 210,615 35 %" for Q3 and nine months (Q3Q p45). CTV is 284,770 of the nine-month total of 551,127. Filings group channels as CTV, Mobile and Desktop; the releases group CTV and DV+ (ER3 p1). The company reports one segment: "operates as one operating segment and one reportable segment" (Q3Q p8).
#### Capital structure at September 30, 2026

- Term loan: "2024 Term Loan B Facility $ 357,730 $ 360,454" (Q3Q p20), secured by substantially all assets, maturing February 2031, contractual rate "6.90%" at September 30, 2026 (Q3Q p19). Carrying value net of discount and issuance costs 349,950 (Q3Q p17).

- Revolver: $175.0 million, undrawn, matures February 2029; "amounts available under the 2024 Revolving Credit Facility were $170.9 million, net of letters of credit outstanding in the amount of $4.1 million" (Q3Q p20).
- Convertible notes: "On March 15, 2026, the Convertible Senior Notes matured" and "No Convertible Senior Notes remained outstanding" (Q3Q p14). Principal repaid 205,067 (cash flow, Q3Q p5).

- Claims outside the debt figure: lease liabilities current 21,558 and non-current 40,436 (Q3Q p2); non-cancelable cloud, software and data center obligations "Total $ 115,219" (Q3Q p22). No pension, factoring or off-balance-sheet financing is described in the sections read; none was found in a search for those terms (see Gaps).

- Covenant: springing First Lien Net Leverage Ratio below 3.25 to 1.00, tested only if revolver utilization exceeds 35% of commitments; no revolver amount outstanding at September 30, 2026 and the Company "was in compliance with its debt covenants" (Q3Q p20). No reported ratio is supplied.
#### Subsequent event

Amendment No. 3 dated October 7, 2026 lowered the term loan margin to Term SOFR plus 2.50% from 3.00% and the revolver margin range from 3.50% to 4.00% to 2.50% to 3.00% (Q3Q p29, p30). It post-dates the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not applied to any figure above.
### Definition risks and quality of earnings

- Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's measure: "Other companies may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently than we do" (10K p100). It adds back stock-based compensation (76,648 in FY2025; 55,805 in nine months 2026), which is a real cost to equity holders but not cash.

- The FY2025 bridge from income from operations to Adjusted EBITDA ties exactly: 97,601 plus D&A 53,674 plus stock compensation 76,648 gives 227,923, and the remaining 4,208 equals merger costs 162, litigation expense 1,116, non-operational real estate and other 890, other income 1,073 and other debt refinancing expense 967. The nine-month 2026 and 2025 bridges also tie (8,665 and 3,796). Other income is included in Adjusted EBITDA because the reconciliation does not deduct it.

- The releases define "Operating cash flow is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA less capital expenditures" (ER3 p2) and free cash flow as that less net interest expense. These are not the cash flow statement's "Net cash provided by operating activities". This answer uses the statement figure for cash flow and labels operating cash flow less capex as a derived measure.

- FY2025 net income of 144,613 includes a tax benefit: "Provision (benefit) for income taxes (73,986)" (10K p120) and deferred taxes of (78,230) in the cash flow statement (10K p121); the auditor's critical audit matters include "Income Taxes — Valuation Allowance Release" (10K p118) and the filing states federal valuation allowances were released (10K p72). Net income is therefore not a run-rate measure; cash taxes paid were 3,760.

- Litigation: Magnite sued Google on September 16, 2025; litigation expense is added back (ER3 p13: "Litigation expense (1) 1,999 527 3,815 1,043"). No recovery or liability is recorded or quantified (Q3Q p24).

- Seasonality and float: "expect these measures to be higher in the fourth quarter than in other quarters" (10K p29); first-quarter 2026 operating cash flow was negative ("net cash used in operating activities was $120.8 million", Q1Q p47). Accounts payable and accrued expenses of 1,738,299 exceed accounts receivable of 1,432,233 (Q3Q p2) because the company collects from buyers and pays publishers. Reported cash and net debt are sensitive to the date within the cycle.
- Guidance (management, attributed): Q4 2026 total Contribution ex-TAC "between $227 million and $233 million" (ER3 p1). It is a management expectation, not used in any ratio.
## Calculations

All inputs are printed figures in US$ thousands from the cited chunks. "LTM" means last twelve months to the stated quarter end, computed as FY2025 plus the 2026 year-to-date figure less the 2025 year-to-date figure.

10. Undrawn FY2024 (derived): $175.0 million less $5.2 million = $169.8 million. Liquidity in the chart is cash plus undrawn facilities shown separately; it is not netted for the minimum cash needed to run the platform.
11. Illustrative effect of Amendment No. 3 (not a company figure): 357,730 x 0.50% = 1,789 per year on the September 30, 2026 principal, before changes in Term SOFR.

### Business and transaction view

Magnite is a public company with no financial sponsor, no controlling holder identified in the supplied sources and a single operating segment. It sells technology that lets publishers, especially connected TV owners, monetize ad inventory to buyers and demand-side platforms, and earns a fee that is a percentage of the ad spend. The credit-relevant business facts are the dependence on a small number of large demand sources, the concentration of connected TV supply in a few large sellers, the lower fees on reserve auctions, seasonal fourth-quarter strength, and the effect of the Google antitrust ruling on open-web display competition. The credit-relevant history is the financing of the SpotX acquisition by a term loan and convertible notes, the 2024 refinancing and repricings, the repayment of the convertible notes in cash at maturity in March 2026, and the October 2026 repricing amendment. There is no pending acquisition, sponsor transaction or new debt issue in the supplied sources. Governance evidence is limited to documented actions: deleveraging by repayment, share repurchases under a board plan and no dividends. The financial consequences are in the accepted financial base handoff; the main limits here are that ownership percentages, the proxy statement and the executed financing documents are not supplied, and that operating claims in the releases are management language.

No acquisition, sponsor transaction, merger, dividend recapitalisation or new debt issue is described in the supplied sources for FY2025 or 2026 to date, other than the items below. Timeline, by date:

- February 6, 2024: refinancing into the 2024 Credit Agreement, a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolver (Q3Q p19). Amendments in September 2024 and March 2025 repriced the term loan to Term SOFR plus 3.00% (Q3Q p19). These are borrower-favourable repricings; they are debt terms, not changes of control.

- September 2025: completed the acquisition of Streamrai, Inc., a generative-AI video-ad tool for connected TV (10K p15). The cash outflow was small relative to the balance sheet (financial base handoff, acquisitions line); purchase terms and price allocation are Not supplied in the chunks read.
- September 16, 2025: filed a lawsuit against Google in the Eastern District of Virginia seeking damages and other remedies; no recovery is recorded and none is quantified (Q3Q p24, p36).
- March 15, 2026: the convertible senior notes matured and were repaid in cash; no convertible notes remain (Q3Q p14). No new debt was raised for this.
- Second quarter 2026: a short-term draw on the revolver was borrowed and repaid within the quarter (Q2Q p18); the revolver was undrawn at quarter ends.

- February 23, 2026 and nine months 2026: the board approved a share repurchase plan, and shares were repurchased under it in the period (Q3Q p50). This returns cash to equity holders; the repurchase capacity under the credit agreement is Not supplied.

- September 2026: the Court issued its remedies opinion against Google ("mandating that Google undertake certain behavioral remedies and appointing a six-year independent compliance monitor"); "Google has indicated its intent to appeal the decision" (Q3Q p36). Management says it expects "a significant positive impact on our industry and business prospects" (Management Language, Q3Q p36). The 2027 outlook is stated "not including upside from Google remedies" (ER3 p1).

- Subsequent event, October 7, 2026: Amendment No. 3 lowered the term loan margin and the revolver margin range (Q3Q p29). It post-dates the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and is not folded into that period's facts.

Governance and sponsor behaviour (issuer level, documented actions only): the repayment of the convertible notes from cash is deleveraging; share repurchases and the prior-period repricings are neutral to supportive; there is no evidence of dividend recapitalisation, debt-funded distribution, priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release in the sources read. Legal capacity (what the credit agreement permits for restricted payments, incurrence and liens), willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and leverage in the financial base) are kept separate: willingness and feasibility are evidenced, legal capacity is not because the credit agreement is Not supplied. Evidence quality is High for the dated filings and Low for management claims in the releases.

Conflicts logged: none. No two supplied documents state a different amount or date for the same fact in the chunks read. The FY2025 10-K debt note first states a 4.50% term loan margin and then the amendments that reduced it to 3.00%; that is a history of terms, not a conflict.
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: revenue is a percentage of ad spend and the take rate "tends to be lower on CTV transactions" (10K p41); results are higher in the fourth quarter (10K p29). Mechanic: growth is volume driven and exposed to ad budgets and to fee compression as connected TV reserve auctions grow. Implication: cash flow is cyclical and seasonal; the financial base shows strong recent growth, but revenue visibility is not contractually evidenced (Insufficient Information on contract terms). The Google remedies are a possible counter-force but are unquantified and under appeal.

2. Concentration risk. Evidence: "two buyers accounted for 40% and 12%" of receivables (10K p137) and demand is "highly concentrated among relatively few DSPs" (10K p25). Mechanic: a payment delay or volume shift at one platform hits both collections and revenue, and Magnite pays sellers regardless. Implication: liquidity and the cash-float qualification matter more than the leverage ratio alone.

3. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor named; no dividends; notes repaid from cash. Mechanic: no sponsor extraction channel is evidenced. Implication: monitor share repurchases against the credit agreement restrictions, which are not supplied.
4. Key uncertainties: executed financing documents, proxy ownership, contract terms and the outcome and timing of the Google remedies and damages claim.

The business is cyclical and concentrated in a few buyers. | Medium | The credit agreement, covenant definitions and ratings are not supplied, and part of the cash is customer float. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Earnings rest on ad spend, connected TV fee mix and two large buyers; the Google remedies are an unquantified upside under appeal. | Cash flow is cyclical; strong recent growth does not remove concentration risk. | Medium |
### Credit view

Magnite is a low-leverage, cash-rich credit with one secured term loan, and the supplied evidence supports a strong but cyclical view with Medium confidence. The strongest support is that gross debt of USD 357,730 thousand is 1.27x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, cash of USD 392,862 thousand exceeds it, the revolver is undrawn and no debt matures before February 2029 [CP-1]. The weakest point is that earnings follow advertising budgets, depend on a few demand platforms and sit beside large seller payables, so reported cash overstates free liquidity [CP-1, CP-1A]. The outcome turns on whether connected TV volume growth outruns fee compression and whether cash returns to shareholders stay modest, and the credit agreement terms that would limit them are not supplied [CP-0].
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | Assessment | Category | Basis |
| Overall | Strong balance sheet, cyclical and concentrated operations | Analyst Interpretation | [CP-1] leverage tables; [CP-1A] operating model |
| Leverage | 1.27x gross and -0.13x net on Adjusted EBITDA at LTM Q3 2026; 1.81x gross after stock compensation | Documentary Fact (derived in CP-1) | [CP-1] financials and credit metrics |
| Liquidity | USD 392,862 thousand cash plus USD 170.9 million undrawn; no maturity in the next twelve months | Documentary Fact | [CP-1] chart data liquidity and maturities |
| Business risk | Single segment, demand concentration, lower fees on connected TV reserve auctions | Documentary Fact | [CP-1A] company and operating model |
| Governance | No named sponsor; notes repaid from cash; share repurchases; legal capacity not evidenced | Analyst Interpretation | [CP-1A] transaction summary |
| Confidence | Medium | Analyst Interpretation | Limited by [CP-0] and the unsupplied credit agreement |
### Key findings

Magnite's capital structure is the simplest part of the credit. Since the convertible senior notes were repaid from cash at maturity on March 15, 2026, the only debt is the 2024 term loan, with principal of USD 357,730 thousand at September 30, 2026, scheduled amortization of USD 3,632 thousand a year, and USD 342,294 thousand falling due after 2030, at the February 2031 maturity [CP-1]. The USD 175.0 million revolver matures in February 2029, was undrawn at every 2026 quarter end, and had USD 170.9 million available after USD 4.1 million of letters of credit. The October 7, 2026 repricing, a subsequent event, cut the term loan margin to Term SOFR plus 2.50%; at the September 30, 2026 principal that is roughly USD 1,789 thousand a year of lower interest before changes in Term SOFR [CP-1, calculation 11].

Earnings have improved sharply. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months to September 30, 2026 is USD 280,586 thousand against USD 232,131 thousand for FY2025, and Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 10.98x [CP-1]. That figure is the issuer's own measure and adds back stock-based compensation; on income from operations plus depreciation and amortization, gross leverage is 1.81x, still low [CP-1]. Reported net income for FY2025 includes a one-off tax benefit of USD 73,986 thousand and should not be read as run-rate.

Cash is the item most open to misreading. The company collects from buyers and pays sellers, and the filing states that "in the event a buyer defaults on payment, we may still be required to pay sellers for the inventory purchased" [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Two buyers made up 40% and 12% of receivables at December 31, 2025 [CP-1A]. Cash fell from USD 553,362 thousand at FY2025 to USD 184,648 thousand at the end of the first quarter, helped by the USD 205,067 thousand note repayment and a negative first-quarter operating cash flow, before recovering to USD 392,862 thousand [CP-1]. Net debt of USD -35,132 thousand is therefore a point-in-time figure, not a permanent surplus.

The leverage covenant is a springing test: First Lien Net Leverage Ratio below 3.25 to 1.00, tested at quarter end only if revolver utilization exceeds 35% of commitments [Q3 2026 10-Q]. Thirty-five percent of USD 175.0 million is USD 61,250 thousand; the USD 60.0 million drawn and repaid within the second quarter of 2026 was just below that level, and whether letters of credit count toward utilization is not stated in the supplied text. Nothing was drawn at quarter end, so the test did not apply. As an indicator only, not the covenant calculation, first-lien debt at the term loan principal would reach 3.25x of LTM Adjusted EBITDA only if that EBITDA fell by about 61%, with cash netting and the covenant EBITDA definition both unknown [CP-0].

Claims outside the debt figure are modest on the evidence: lease liabilities of USD 21,558 thousand current and USD 40,436 thousand non-current, and non-cancelable cloud, software and data center commitments of USD 115,219 thousand, of which USD 78,343 thousand falls in 2027 [CP-1, Q3 2026 10-Q]. No pension, factoring or consent-decree obligation was found in the sections read. The Google lawsuit is a possible recovery, with nothing recorded, and the court's September 2026 remedies are under appeal [CP-1A]; guidance for 2027 excludes any upside from them.

Management's board-approved repurchase plan has USD 144.9 million of authorization left [Q3 2026 10-Q], and USD 55,559 thousand of treasury stock was purchased in the nine months to September 30, 2026 [Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement]. This is the main route by which cash could leave the credit; the restricted-payment limits in the credit agreement are not supplied [CP-0, CP-1A].
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are balance-sheet capacity and growth momentum. Gross leverage of 1.27x on Adjusted EBITDA, net cash after the March 2026 repayment, an undrawn USD 175.0 million revolver, no maturity before 2029 and interest cover of 10.98x leave wide room against the one springing covenant [CP-1]. Operating momentum is strong: Contribution ex-TAC for nine months 2026 was USD 551,127 thousand against USD 474,583 thousand a year earlier, led by connected TV [CP-1]. The absence of a financial sponsor, dividends or debt-funded distributions in the sources read, and the repayment of the convertible notes without new borrowing, are supportive behaviours [CP-1A]. The Google ruling is a potential tailwind to open-web display share, though it is management's expectation, unquantified and under appeal.

The main weaknesses are cyclicality, concentration and unverified terms. Revenue is a percentage of ad spend, with lower fees on connected TV reserve auctions, so growth in the fastest channel can dilute the fee rate [CP-1A]. Demand is concentrated in a few platforms and two buyers hold over half of receivables, so a payment delay or loss would hit revenue and cash together. Cash includes publisher and customer float, seasonality lifts the fourth quarter, and first-quarter cash flow can be negative [CP-1]. Adjusted EBITDA excludes stock compensation of USD 76,648 thousand in FY2025. The credit agreement, covenant definitions, restricted-payment capacity, guarantor list and ratings are not supplied, so legal capacity to add debt or distribute cash cannot be tested [CP-0, CP-1A]. Business is one segment, so no other activity offsets a weak ad market.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Advertising cycle and fee compression | Revenue is a share of ad spend; connected TV reserve auctions carry lower fees | Earnings and interest cover fall together in a downturn, but low leverage gives a wide buffer | Material |
| Buyer concentration and payment default | Magnite pays sellers even if a large buyer does not pay; two buyers hold most receivables | Cash and liquidity could fall faster than earnings | Material |
| Cash returned to shareholders | Repurchase authorization of USD 144.9 million remains; limits not supplied | Net cash could erode if repurchases accelerate | Minor |
| Unverified covenant and document terms | Credit agreement and definitions not supplied | Headroom and legal capacity cannot be certified | Material |
| Google litigation and remedies | Appeal pending; damages claim unquantified | Upside and legal cost both uncertain | Minor |
## Calculations
All inputs are from the accepted handoffs or cited filing chunks, in US$ thousands unless stated.

1. Revolver utilization trigger: 35% x USD 175,000 thousand = USD 61,250 thousand (Q3Q p20 for the 35% and 175.0 million commitment). Q2 2026 draw: USD 60,000 thousand, equal to 34.3% of commitments (60,000 / 175,000). Whether letters of credit of USD 4,100 thousand add to utilization (which would give 36.6%) is not stated.

2. Indicator headroom, not the covenant: 357,730 / 3.25 = 110,071 of EBITDA at which gross term loan leverage equals 3.25x; 1 - 110,071 / 280,586 = 60.8% fall from LTM Adjusted EBITDA (280,586 from CP-1). The covenant ratio is net of cash and uses a defined EBITDA, both unknown.
3. Total liquidity components shown separately, not netted for float: cash 392,862 plus undrawn revolver 170,900 = 563,762.
4. Lease liabilities: 21,558 + 40,436 = 61,994 (Q3Q p2).
5. All other figures are from CP-1 (leverage 1.27x and 1.81x, net debt -35,132, cover 10.98x, LTM Adjusted EBITDA 280,586) and are not recomputed.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affects | Action |

| Credit agreement, amendments, covenant definitions and a reported First Lien Net Leverage Ratio are Not supplied | Material | Headroom, restricted-payment and incurrence capacity | Retrieve the exhibits listed in the 10-K exhibit index if headroom matters |
| Free cash versus customer and publisher float is Not supplied | Material | True liquidity | Treat reported cash as an upper bound |
| Contract terms with demand platforms and large sellers are Not supplied [CP-1A] | Material | Revenue visibility | None in the filings read |
| Ratings and market data: context fields empty | Minor for this view | External view | None |
| Discrete Q4 2025 is not reported; Q4 2026 guidance is a management expectation | Minor | Seasonal run-rate | Treat as derived or management view |
| Ownership percentages, proxy statement, guarantor names | Minor | Control and guarantee structure | Retrieve proxy and Exhibit 21 |
| Source form: text extraction without XBRL [CP-0] | Minor | Layout checks | Figures re-read against cited chunks |
## Next module

Proceed to the evidence review. It should test: the 1.27x and 1.81x leverage readings against the cited statements; the 40% and 12% receivable concentration; the 61% indicator headroom, which depends on assumptions flagged above; the cash-float qualification; and that the October 7, 2026 amendment and the September 2026 Google remedies are treated as events of their stated dates.
